scope.description: One exact published Canada Rocket Company refresh covering legal identity, ownership, financing, current technical activity, R-series/E-1 detail and bounded government and investor records.

source.title: Canada Rocket Company R-Series and E-1 product overview
source.locator: R-1, R-2, E-1, team and contact sections
source.summary: The official site describes the R-1 pathfinder, seven-engine R-2 concept, E-1 methalox engine, shared architecture, intended launch uses, public email and Etobicoke address.

leads.evidenceLocator: Corporations Canada, DND and NRC agreements, BDC investment records, CRC product pages, House testimony, SpaceQ and IEEE Spectrum
followUpQuestions: Which current R-2 payload, orbit, staging and reuse baseline should a prospective mission planner evaluate?
Which E-1 thrust rating and completed component, gas-generator or full-engine test evidence defines the current propulsion baseline?
Which test-site and launch-site agreements, Transport Canada approvals and launch-licensing milestones are executed rather than under discussion?
How does the current R-2 emphasis change the deliverables, schedule and light-lift outcome attached to IDEaS agreement CO5-023?
reviewWarnings: Current R-2 payload claims conflict across company, parliamentary and industry sources: 6,500 kilograms to 500-kilometre LEO, 12,500 kilograms with mixed or unstated orbit basis, and 12,000 to 15,000 kilograms to LEO; none is flight validated.
Current company-controlled E-1 descriptions vary between 700, 725 and 750 kilonewtons; no versioned data sheet or completed hot-fire result reconciles the design baseline.

No reviewed durable source establishes a completed component-test result, gas-generator or full-engine hot-fire, vehicle flight, launch licence, selected launch site, customer booking, manifested payload, accepted delivery or operational service.
DND agreement CO5-023 is a C$8,333,333 development grant tied to R1/light-lift work, not a procurement contract, completed prototype, flight, acceptance or fielding record.
NRC IRAP agreement 1041206 funds defence procurement and cybersecurity readiness; it does not establish procurement eligibility, certification, customer interest or successful project completion.

C$6.2 million, C$14.7 million, C$22.5 million and C$22.8 million figures use different dates and public bases; they are not summed, and exact current ownership percentages and the post-financing cap table remain undisclosed.
Telesat appears as payload-sizing context, not a customer, reservation or partner; reported test-site and launch-site arrangements remain undisclosed access or partnership discussions.
Controlled Goods Program registration is not a procurement award, product approval, security clearance, export authorization or evidence of eligibility for a specific acquisition.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Confirmed the current R-1, R-2 and E-1 architecture, public contact and the internal R-2 payload conflict on the official product surface.
Confirmed the active federal legal entity, 2025 incorporation, registered office, directors and disclosed direct-control bands.
Confirmed agreement CO5-023, its C$8,333,333 value, dates, legal recipient and light-lift development purpose.
Confirmed NRC IRAP agreement 1041206 and its C$75,000 defence procurement and cybersecurity-readiness scope without inferring qualification.
Confirmed BDC's 2025 Seed Venture Fund relationship and the separate C$6.2 million co-led round announcement.
Confirmed the August R-2 emphasis, 12,000-to-15,000-kilogram projection, late-2027 engine static-fire expectation and years-to-orbit boundary.
Confirmed preliminary turbopump work, the Etobicoke facility, undisclosed test site, launch-site discussions and absence of a completed hot-fire or flight.
Searched CanadaBuys, Transport Canada launch-licensing and public customer records; no CRC procurement award, launch licence, booking or manifested payload was located.
Searched CIPO and public patent records under the company, legal entity and principals; no attributable CRC patent or technical filing was located.
Confirmed the French DND Launch the North surface and French-interface NRC record; they added terminology but no different decision-changing facts.

leads.refreshSummary: Canada Rocket Company is proposed to update current activity to the August 2026 R-2 emphasis, set legal name and disclosed financing, revise the R-series/E-1 capability, and add CO5-023, NRC 1041206 and BDC records while preserving the 6,500 versus 12,000-to-15,000-kilogram conflict.
